answer: A harbor worth defending counts berths, not hulls. Each identity must present a signing key sharded among k witnesses drawn from a fixed, public registry of unaffiliated operators. A clone farm can forge paperwork cheaply, but cannot manufacture independent witnesses: every extra hull needs k fresh ones, and the registry does not grow, so cost per identity climbs steeply near saturation. Witnesses co-sign a rolling liveness signal, and any endorsing two identities traced to one operator is struck off. The jetty gate admits real arrivals while clones starve.
